Overall: 8/10.

Story & Plot

Following a tragic car crash that claims the life of her boyfriend, piano student Laura is taken in by Betty, a witness to the accident who nurses her back to health. Living with Betty's family in the German countryside offers initial comfort, but as time passes, Laura begins to question their true intentions. Christian Petzold's enigmatic drama explores themes of letting go, unfolding with meandering mysteries and a quiet, unassuming resolution.

Comedy & Entertainment

While the film is an enigmatic drama rather than a traditional comedy, it offers a fascinating and highly diverting study of an unhappy family group. Its entertainment value stems from Petzoldian alienation and a strangely restorative, sun-dappled noir atmosphere. The tension arises from the psychological dynamics between characters rather than any humorous moments.

Performances & Direction

Paula Beer delivers a magnificent lead performance as a troubled young woman who feels something is missing in her life. She is strongly supported by Petzold regulars Barbara Auer and Matthias Brandt in their roles as parents deeply scarred by the death of their child. The main cast also features Enno Trebs and Philip Froissant, all contributing to the film's affecting portrayals.

Strengths

  • Compact and masterful direction by Christian Petzold
  • Magnificent, affecting lead performance by Paula Beer
  • Engaging exploration of letting go and mystery
  • Atmospheric sun-dappled noir style
  • Strong supporting performances from Barbara Auer and Matthias Brandt

Weaknesses

Some viewers may find that the film does not fully deliver on all of its narrative promises, featuring a quiet resolution and a rejection of traditional narrative climaxes. The meandering mysteries and pacing could leave audiences wanting a more conventional payoff. It treads familiar psychological ground that might feel somewhat constrained to those looking for faster-paced thrills.

Final verdict

Christian Petzold has crafted another compact, elegant, and enigmatic drama that rewards patient viewers with strong acting and atmospheric tension. While its quiet resolution and unconventional narrative choices may not satisfy everyone, its masterclass in tone and performance makes it a worthwhile watch. Recommended for fans of thoughtful European drama and psychological mysteries.
